items.action: Include headline and bold it or make it a larger font than others.

items.title: Headline is niche-specific and contains benefit and timeframe?
items.action: Make sure the headline calls out a specific niche. Example: For [Niche]: How to get [result] in [timeframe] without [something they don't want].

items.title: Opt-In explanation steps contain "how tos" or steps?
items.action: The steps or curiosity hooks are under the headline and speak to the content within the asset. Example: In this paper you will learn : 1. How to get [benefit] without [cost] 2. The relatively unknown method to get [benefit] without [cost]. 3. How to [get result] without [cost] in [timeframe] 4. The easiest and most effective way to [get result] without [cost].

items.title: Image exists that is relevant and clear?
items.action: The image needs to intrigue someone and take action. Typically this is a proof shot or testimonial. For example: An image of a customer's and a quote. An image of a customer's data improvements (before and after). You can also include an image of you on stage or an image of you. You can also include a short video of you welcoming someone to the page and explaining the copy on the page and routing them to the call to action.

items.title: CTA is clear?
items.action: The cta needs to be contrasted and clear and speak to the verb above the headline. For example: if someone is downloading an asset, the cta should read, "Download Now" or "Get Asset". The congruence is key.

items.title: Social proof exists?
items.action: Social proof can be in the form of logos, team, case studies or all of the above. In general, the more social proof, the better.

items.title: Opt-in cta causes a pop-up to lead capture?
items.action: On an opt-in, you want to create as little friction as possible. Tools like clickfunnels or other pages allow for quick and easy pop-ups to capture leads. You want to capture the name and email and(optional) phone number.

items.title: Logo exists?

items.title: Background image is pleasant?
items.action: The background image sets the tone of the page. It's best to use a picture that depicts positive emotions and generates excitement.

items.title: Spacing of assets makes sense?
items.action: Get a designer or use your own eye to make sure the spacing of the elements on the page is visually appealing. Weird spacing can reduce the conversion rate.

items.title: Images are large enough?
items.action: Make sure the images and the text in the image is large enough so that the viewer is not frustrated when viewing. A frustrated viewer is less likely to convert than a non-frustrated viewer.

items.title: Text on the page is consistent and large enough font?
items.action: Ensure the text on the page is consistent and the font size is large enough such that the viewer doesn't need to squint or work to read.

items.title: Page loads quickly?
items.action: Test the page and make sure the page loads fast. Properly size images so that they load quickly, but don't sacrifice image quality.

items.title: Page loads on mobile?
items.action: Test on mobile and with other browsers to ensure there are no technical issues or weird spacing.

items.title: Status delta is achieved?
items.action: Use tonality, pacing, and language patterns + social proof.

items.title: Agenda is stated?
items.action: State agenda. This helps the prospect stay on track and keeps their answers concise.

items.title: Questions are asked?
items.action: Ask qualification questions. Recall that qualification qualifies for money, authority, and problem/need.

items.title: Prospect listens to answers and takes notes?
items.action: Listen intensely and take notes. Show the prospect that you are taking notes.

items.title: Rep determines root cause?
items.action: Try to determine the root cause of their problem. Update in your notes. Be as detailed as possible. This will help the closer or you on the closing call.

items.title: Rep validates that the prospect has decision-making authority?
items.action: Validate that the prospect has decision-making authority by asking how decisions are made.

items.title: Rep does not solve problems on the call?
items.action: Don't try to solve a problem on the call. Remember that all you are doing is qualifying.

items.title: Rep pitches benefits on the call/sizzle?
items.action: If the prospect is qualified, pitch the benefit and give a few case studies. Don't pitch the "how" or "what" at all.

items.title: Rep introduces benefits of showing up for demo call?
items.action: Give a few reasons why the prospect needs to show up for the demo call. Frame it as a benefit to them. For example: "On the call, we will walk through the action plan and help you as much as possible for free."

items.title: Rep doesn't pitch features and offer on the call?
items.action: Don't pitch the features/"how" or "what".

items.title: Rep presents multiple timeslots within the week?
items.action: When presenting the timeslots to the prospect, give multiple slots. Don't ask questions like "what time works for you?"

items.title: Rep qualifies for price?
items.action: Give a price range and see if the prospect is able to handle that price with a question like: "The typical engagement with us ranges from X to Y. If we could solve a meaningful problem for you and get you results, is the company able to invest?"

items.title: Rep requests that decision makers are on demo call?
items.action: Remind the prospect that decision-makers should be on the call. Politely tell them: "It's best that decision-makers on the call, this will allow us to get to conclusion asap."

items.title: Rep introduces salesperson?
items.action: If you are booking the demo on a salesperson's calendar, introduce the salesperson and frame them as the expert.

items.title: Rep takes detailed notes in CRM?
items.action: Remember to take detailed notes in the CRM. This helps the closer on the other side. If you are doing the call, this will help you recal important facts quickly which frames you properly.

items.title: Rep updates status in CRM?
items.action: Update the status in the CRM after the call. Opportunity status and lead status.

items.title: Rep sends thank you note after the call?
items.action: Thank the prospect for the time after the call with an email. Adding that extra touch point will increase the show up rate and close rate.

items.title: If rep is requested to demo, the rep explains the benefits.
items.action: If the prospect asks about how you help, give a simple explanation of the benefits. Sell the sizzle, not the steak. Present case studies and drop social proof.

items.title: Rep presents case studies?
items.action: Provide the prospect with case studies and social proof and get the status delta. The status delta carries into the entire presentation and helps increase the close rate.

items.action: Get contact information from decision-makers and send video sales letters and notes on the call.

items.title: All reps are filling out content sheets?
Demo completed not closed list exists?
Product training watched at least 5 times?
Sales Process Training watched at least 5 times?
Intro made to other salespeople and managers?
Sales script written out by hand 10 times?
Information is sent to customer before the sales call for prospect to "marinate"?
items.action: Send customer information (VSLs, written sales letters, case studies) before call. Personalize as much as possible.

items.title: Connected with prospect on LinkedIn or Facebook?
items.action: Connect with prospect over LinkedIn and Facebook. Make sure you have content on your page that speaks to benefits of the offer.

items.title: Stretching was done before call?
items.action: Before call, stretch and get limber. This will keep your voice sounding smooth and deep and keep you calm during the call.

items.title: Research was done before the call? Notes were reviewed?
items.action: Review the prospect's notes before the call. The SDR or MRR or you should have detailed discovery notes in CRM or answers from the quiz. You can comment on answers before the call to increase engagement.

items.title: Confirmation email sent immediately after prospect books call?
items.action: Send out a confirmation email after prospect books asking the prospect to confirm. You can do this with a text or automated email with zapier. This is just another touch point that increases show-up rates on the call and increases engagement. It also shows the prospect that you are on the ball.

items.title: Confirmation message includes benefits as to why the prospect should show up?
items.action: Make sure the confirmation message includes benefits relative to prospect. This increases show up rate. If the prospect doesn't have a good reason to show up, they are less likely to do so. Benefits could include: Free consulting call, free strategy call, free audit on process. Try to provide value here.

items.title: Confirmation message is sent within 30 minutes of prospect filling out questionnaire?
items.action: Make sure a confirmation is sent to prospect as soon as the prospect fills out the questionnaire if they are an inbound prospect. This shows the prospect that you are on the ball. Make the confirmation personalized to something in the questionnaire.

items.title: Quiz confirmation message is personalized?
items.action: Personalize the response as much as possible with the notes or data from the questionnaire.

items.title: Confirmation message include demo itinerary?
items.action: Include an itinerary in the message. This shows the prospect that you know what you are doing. Example: First we are going to cover ___, then ___, then ___. Make sure to include benefits.

items.title: Call is confirmed the morning of the demo call?
items.action: Send a confirmation message in the morning before the call. This provides another touchpoint and reminds the prospect. Keep it simple and casual. You can also text the prospect.

items.title: Reminder email is sent 1 hour before call time and 10 minutes before call time?
items.action: Send a reminder email 1 hour before the call. This can be done with Calendly or your calendar software. Keep it simple and casual.

items.title: Reschedule template exists in CRM?
items.action: If the prospect no shows or needs to reschedule send the prospect a reschedule email. Make sure to keep it friendly and polite. Be unaffected as possible. Include a reschedule link in the email.

items.title: If prospect no shows or cancels, send over reschedule template and mark "demo no show" in CRM.
items.action: If the prospect reschedules or no shows, change the opportunity status in the CRM to "Demo No Show" or "Demo Booked" if they rescheduled.

items.title: Humor was used in emails?
items.action: Use some humor in the email if possible. This increases engagement rate and show up rate. If you can make someone laugh, they will want to speak to you.

items.title: Attend the call 2-3 minutes before prospect?
items.action: Attend the call a few minutes before the prospect and make sure you are ready.

items.title: Script was followed for language patterns during call?
items.action: Follow the script to a tee during the call. Use the slide deck. You want to focus on the performance instead of the content. The script is your best friend.

items.title: Zoom waiting room enabled?
items.action: Enable zoom waiting room feature so you are not caught off guard by the prospect if they enter the zoom room without you knowing.

items.title: Allow prospect to enter call precisely at call scheduled time?
items.action: Allow the prospect into the waiting room at the exact time. This will create status delta on the call.

items.title: Ask prospect if recording call is okay?
items.action: Ask the prospect if recording is okay. Justify by saying that you can send them a recording of the call afterwards if other team members require it.

items.title: Status delta set with intro or tonality?
items.action: Open up and get right down to business. Don't use too much small talk. The prospect needs to know that this is a buying call. Have complete certainty in this section. "Alright, so here's how these call usually go. First I'll ask you some questions, then I'll see if there is a solution we can provide, then I'll present one to you, then I'll ask you to move forward when we come to terms." Use silence here.

items.title: Status delta built by using bullets of case studies and alignments were stated in 1?
items.action: Drop some status delta here with your number of customers, some key case studies, some achievements, alignments. Don't worry about going too far here. You need status delta for the prospect to listen.

items.title: Prospect reminded to keep answers concise?
items.action: Politely ask the prospect to keep the answers to questions concise so that you can quickly determine if there is a fit or not.

items.title: Qualified what piqued interest?
items.action: Ask the prospect what pique their interest using question tonality.

items.title: Qualified current state and activities?
items.action: Ask the prospect questions about their current activities and current state. Don't let the prospect get off the rails by telling stories.

items.title: Qualification questions determined desired state?
items.action: Ask the prospect questions about their goals and their desires. What are they trying to do? Let the prospect open up?

items.title: Qualification questions determined the reason why prospect wasn't at desired state?
items.action: Ask the prospect why in their own opinion they are not hitting their goal. This causes the prospect to think about the root causes and gives you intell on the "hot buttons" that you will focus on during the pitch.

items.title: Rep didn't try to solve problems during qualification?
items.action: Don't try to solve problems during qualification. This derails the pitch and puts things out of order, making it hard to get the prospect back on track.

items.title: Rep qualified for money?
items.action: Explain that the cost to working with you is X and before you continue, they can afford to "make investment" or "pay". If the prospect tells you that they are unable to afford the solution, politely redirect them to another place and end the call.

items.title: Rep qualified for decision-making authority?
items.action: Ask the prospect if they have the ability to make a buying a decision. If they don't ask how are decisions made? If you don't have a buyer on the call, try to line up a call with the buyer. If you are talking to an influencer, you can still pitch the benefits and how it works, however, don't give an offer. Try to determine a problem/solution fit.

items.title: Rep made it clear that a decision was to be made on the call today?
items.action: Get your first test close in by asking them to buy on before you even explain anything. In general, you need 7-9 "nos" so you might as well get the first one out of the way ASAP. This might jar the prospect a little, but that's okay. It just reminds them that they are on a buying call and this makes them more likely to close.

items.title: Prospect didn't get too off track with stories? Answers were concise?
items.action: If the prospects gets off the rails with stories, politely interject after they end a sentence and ask them another question. Don't clash with the prospect or offend them. This may take a little practice. Remember that time is valuable and you don't want to waste either your time or the prospect's time.

items.title: Rep didn't talk much during qualification? Mostly prospect?
items.action: Make sure that the prospect did most of the talking during qualification. If you start yapping, you won't get intel and you might mis-diagnose. You also won't develop rapport with the prospect.

items.title: Rep didn't solve problems during qualification?
items.action: Don't solve problems during qualification. Let the prospect speak and gather information. If you solve problems during qualification, things will get off track and the frame will break.

items.title: Rep was able to identify the root cause or problem?
Transition completed?
items.action: Transition by saying either, "Based on what I hear, we can help you." or "Based on what I learned, what we do here is a great fit for you." If the prospect is not a great fit, say "based on what I learned, what we do here is not the best fit. However, what I recommend is ____".

items.title: Silence used after transition?
items.action: Use silence after the transition. Usually 2-3 seconds.

items.title: Thesis points introduced?
items.action: Introduce thesis points in summary table or diagram. Determine how much the prospect knows about the thesis by walking through it.

items.title: Thesis point contains benefits and "money shots" or proof?
items.action: Make sure thesis point contains benefits and "money shots".

items.title: Rep used enthusiasm when explaining the thesis points?
items.action: Use enthusiasm when explaining the thesis points and benefits. This will excite the prospect.

items.title: Rep confirmed that prospect bought into the thesis and certainty was preserved?
items.action: Confirm that prospect bought into the "method" or "thesis steps" by asking "does this make sense?" or "what part of the process makes the most sense?".

items.title: Transition into "How it works" present?
items.action: Transition into the "how it works" after the prospect has agreed to the "method" or "thesis steps".

items.title: How it works explained? Solution explained in chronological order?
items.action: Explain "How it works" using the steps discussed in the "method" section or "thesis step section."

items.title: Demonstrations were used to present features?
items.action: Use live demonstrations as you are presenting the "how it works". Show as much contrast as possible (jump between old way and old result and new way and new result).

items.title: Tonality was enthusiastic during how it works section?
items.action: Use enthusiastic tonality during "how it works" section. Get the prospect fired up. This is an emotional sell as much as a logical sell.

items.title: Benefits of each feature were explained as rep travelled through how it works?
items.action: Explain benefits as you are walking through each of the features. Better, faster, cheaper than X.

items.title: Thesis point covered if needed during how it works step.
items.action: Reference a thesis step or method step as you are explaining the feature.

items.title: Rep confirmed that prospect agreed that the solution solved problem?
items.action: Get the prospect to buy into the solution by asking "How do you see this working for you?" "What specific part do you see making the biggest impact?"

items.title: Rep anchored the offer to a high price?
items.action: Before the offer is stated, anchor to a higher alternative price. This anchor price should be around 10x the asking price.

items.title: Rep compared the offer to alternatives?
items.action: Don't provide random anchor price. Anchor to alternatives.

items.title: Rep injected some scarcity?
items.action: Use scarcity by giving a limited time or limited spots available.

items.title: Rep introduced the offer with enthusiasm?
items.action: Introduce first offer with enthusiasm.

items.title: Rep stacked the features of the offer and reiterated the benefits of each feature with enthusiasm?
items.action: Stack features of the offer with a slide deck or reference. Reiterate benefits as you are stacking. Use enthusiasm when you are stacking. Get the prospect fired up.

items.title: Rep introduced the price with complete certainty and paused?
items.action: Introduce price with certainty. Do not budget. Pause and let sit for a few seconds. You are expecting the first resistance right now.

items.title: Salesperson asked for close with certainty and rep used a closing line?
items.action: Ask for the close after the first offer is made. You are not expecting to get the deal at this point, but you need the first "no".

items.title: First no/resistance was achieved?
items.action: Get the first no or "maybe".

items.title: Deflection and reposition with product? Prospect agrees that solution fits?
items.action: Explain how exactly the prospect will benefit by referencing the most painful problem that you can solve and go for the close again.

items.title: Salesperson asked for close after second resistance?
items.action: Ask for close after the second offer. Make sure you use language like "it's just a matter of getting some simple information. What do you say? Is it a bad idea to start working together?"

items.title: Deflection and reposition with company?
items.action: After more resistance, go back through case studies and social proof. Reposition the company as an industry leader. Ask for the close again, and make sure that a closing line was used.

items.title: Salesperson asked for close after third resistance?
items.action: Ask for the close after the third offer. Use a closing line.

items.title: Deflection and reposition with personal background?
items.action: After more resistance, go back through your personal story and why it's best that you work you. Ask for another close.

items.title: Salesperson asked for close after fourth resistance?
items.action: Ask for a the close after the fourth offer. Use a closing line.

items.title: Second offer and bonus offered?
items.action: If more resistance, reposition with a second offer that include a bonus. Ask for the close.

items.title: Rep asked for close after 5th resistance?
items.action: Ask for the close again, use another closing pattern.

items.title: Another offer offered?
items.action: If more resistance, reposition with another offer that offers more bonus. Ask for the close.

items.title: Rep asked for close after 6th resistance?
items.action: Ask for the sale again with another closing line. Remain certain.

items.title: Incentive based pricing presented?
items.action: Offer incentive-based pricing to introduce urgency. Make sure to justify the reason why incentive-based pricing is being used.

items.title: incentive-based pricing was justified?
items.action: Always justify an offer with a reason. Typical incentive-based pricing offers are justified by the cost of the back and forth and the cost of the uncertainty.

items.title: Rep asked for close after 7th resistance?
items.action: Ask for the close again using another closing pattern.

items.title: Another offer with different terms offered?
items.action: Offer the offer with different payment terms. For example, if you offered upfront, you can break the payments into 2 or 3 payments. Make sure to always justify the reason why you making a new offer.

items.title: New offer was justified?
items.action: Give justification for new offer and better terms. Could be that you need to hit your numbers for the month, or that you can beat a co-worker in a competition. Some reason. Don't just give no reason for close.

items.title: Rep asked for close after 8th resistance?
items.action: Ask for the sale again with another closing line. Remain certain.

items.title: Trial presented or zero risk offer presented?
items.action: Trial offer was offered as last resort to get a customer in today. A $1 trial or a $0 trial was offered. This is used to ring out any other objections the prospect may have. A closing line was introduced here.

items.title: Rep asked for close after 9th resistance?
items.action: Ask for the close again.

items.title: Tonality was certain?
items.action: Make sure to use certain tonality during the close at all times.

items.title: Certainty was used during credit card or contract process and salesperson didn't stumble?
items.action: Don't stumble or squeak during the collection of the credit card or payment terms. You need to remain 100% certain.

items.title: Humor was used to break tension?
items.action: If you can make the prospect laugh at this point, they will likely fall over into the end zone.

items.title: Worst case scenario pattern was used?
items.action: You can use patterns like "Worst case you ____, best case we ____. What do you say?"

items.title: Strategic silence was used and closing patterns were used?
items.action: Use strategic silence if you need to and make your guarantee.

sections.name: Follow Up If No Close Same Day

items.title: Follow up email sent out with bullets and follow up call was booked?
items.action: Send a recap email to the prospect immediately after the call.

items.title: References sent over?
items.action: Make sure that references were sent in the recap email only if the demo was positive.

items.title: Personal content sent over?
items.action: Send over some more content that the prospect may find useful in the recap email.

items.title: 2 offers were sent over in email same day and day after?
items.action: Send another offer 3-4 hours after your call - better terms or better price. Pull carpet.

items.title: Language was certain in email?
items.action: Make sure to use certain language in the follow-up emails and stipulate the benefits as to why the prospect needs to act now.

items.title: Notes updated in CRM?
items.action: Update notes in CRM.

items.title: Salesperson genuinely tried to help customer?
items.action: Language and tonality was used to genuinely try to help the customer.

items.title: If closed, salesperson immediately asked for referrals?
items.action: Ask for referrals right after you get the close. This is when the prospect is most likely to give someone they know. They might say something like "well, if I get results, I will give you x,y,z" try to get those names for a demo.

items.title: No hesitation existed during objection handling?
items.action: If stumbling happened during the objection handling phase, learn the script and objections better by doing script wars with a partner. There should be no hesitation with an objection or question. The language used here should be "great question...." "100% ..." "this is exactly what my last customer said. This is how we helped them..." Remember that you never lose your positive attitude when you are closing. Everything the prospect says is a good thing! Don't get affected by a roadblock or a problem that you need to solve.

items.title: Salesperson used the cadence: "Great question most of of our customers said the same thing, here's what we did for them..." to handle objections and questions.
items.action: Every objection or deflection contains a language pattern that doesn't clash with the prospect. If you clash or jar the prospec, the red flags will go up and you will blow the call and the deal. Always use a velvet glove approach by ducking and slipping objections. Don't meet the prospect head on and clash ever. Even when you are in a less-than-ideal state, remain positive.

items.title: Salesperson was generally in a good mood?
items.action: Staying in a positive mood is important. Even if you feel like crap, it's important to stay in the positive mood and at least sound you are like in a positive mood. You can do this by ACTING and using inflections and patterns.

items.action: Follow up with the prospect each day for at least 7 times. The money is made in the follow up. This will sometimes annoy the prospect, but who cares. You want to get the no as fast as possible so you can move onto the next prospects. Be ruthless with your follow ups. Text messages, emails, and phone calls are used here.

items.title: Ads are getting rejected
items.action:
Ensure that you’re following all Facebook policies (https://www.facebook.com/policies/ads/) 

If you are following the rules then hover to the ad that was rejected see the reason. Make edits and publish the ad again. 

If they are disapproved again and you are sure that you follow FB policies, submit an ad for manual review.

items.title: Ads not receiving any impressions / not spending
items.action:
Wait 24 hours to see if the ads are getting any impressions.  

If you have waited 24 hours and you still have no impressions then check all of your settings are correct (daily budget at, Ads are approved, Targeting is correct, Placements are correct, Fanpage is
connected, Conversion objective is correct, Bidding is set to auto, etc.)

If everything is set up correctly and still not receiving any impression, duplicate the campaign and publish it again.

items.title: Ads are not receiving any clicks
items.action:
Firstly make sure that ads are receiving impressions, if not then see the previous step and troubleshoot it there. 

If your ads are receiving impressions but not receiving clicks then first check all your settings to make sure they are correct and align with the training covered in the Advertising module. 

If your setup and settings are in alignment with the training then you want to check how many impressions you have in total compared
to the 0 number of clicks. If your impressions are above 1,000 and clicks at 0 or near 0 then there’s a high chance Facebook cut off traffic to your ad because it didn’t evoke a response from the audiences you selected. 

Delete all your adsets and launch your campaign again following our launch process. 

If the same issue occurs again then you have a serious issue
with your messaging and audience selection and you need to go back to the drawing board to come up with new ideas/ad copies/images.

items.title: CPM is high
items.action:
If your Cost per 1k impressions (CPM) is outside of KPI then you want to take a look at these metrics: CPC, CTR, and Ad quality metrics. 

If your CPC is within KPI but your CPM is outside of KPI this can be ok and nothing to worry about. 

If your CPC is outside of KPI along with your CPM, this means that your niche isn't resonating with your ads well enough to make it efficient to advertise to them. If this is the case you need to test additional ad copies, images, and audience interests.

Also, some countries have generally higher CPM than the others (USA, Canada, UK, Australia, UK have higher CPM than countries in Asia, Africa, South America...)

items.title: Cost per Quiz is high
items.action:
Before determining your Cost Per Quiz, you must have a significant number of quiz visits and quizzes completed to see what exactly is the problem.

If you have enough quiz visits then you may need to check whether your CPC, CTR, and CPM are inside/outside of KPI. 

If your CPQ is outside of KPI but your ROI is still 2:1 or above then this might not be an issue to worry about since your campaign is still profitable. 

If your ROI is below 2:1 then proceed with the following:


If you DON'T have enough quiz visits that means that your VSL is not resonating with your audience. 

This is probably due to inconsistent messaging between your ads/landing page and your VSL. 

If this problem persists you need to keep iterating your VSL until you can get your cost per quiz within KPI.

items.title: CPA is outside of KPI's
items.action:
Before judging your CPA it’s important to solve all these metrics (CPC, CTR, CPM, VSL conversion rate, Quiz conversion rate, Call conversion and show up raterate). 

CPA is a function of all of the previous metrics combined into one and if any of them are outside of KPI they will be reflecting in your CPA figure.

items.title: ROI is outside of KPI's
items.action:
ROI is a function of all of the previous metrics combined into one and if any of them are outside of KPI they will be reflecting in your ROI figure. 

If all of your metrics are within KPI except for ROI then this can be any of the following things: Poorly priced offering and/or Hyper competitive market.

items.title: Ads Learning limited phase
items.action:
If your ad set isn't getting enough optimisation events to exit the learning phase, the Delivery column reads learning limited. Learning limited isn't a penalty – it's an indication that your budget isn't being spent effectively because the ad delivery system can't optimise performance with your current setup.

An ad set becomes learning limited when it is unlikely to receive around 50 optimisation events in the week after your last significant edit. This diagnosis can happen any time after you create an ad set or make a significant edit to an existing one.

Generally, an ad set becomes learning limited when the ad set is limited by small audience size, low budget, low bid or cost control, high auction overlap, an infrequent optimisation event, or other issues such as running too many ads at the same time. If an ad set is limited by a low bid or cost control, a tooltip will appear when you hover over the learning limited status.


There are multiple ways to fix learning limited ad sets to improve performance.

- Combine ads sets and campaigns. Combining ad sets and campaigns will help you get the results you need faster, which means you'll see stable results sooner.
- Expand your audience. The larger the audience, the more opportunities for people to complete your optimisation event.
- Raise your budget. If your budget is too low to receive around 50 optimisation events, the ad set is unlikely to exit the learning phase.
- Raise your bid or cost control. If your bid or cost control is too low to receive around 50 optimisation events, the ad set is unlikely to exit the learning phase.
- Change your optimisation event. Consider choosing an optimisation event that occurs more frequently. For example, move from purchases to add to cart.

If a learning limited ad set receives 50 optimisation events since your last significant edit, it will move from learning limited to active.
